components.name: Library rail

components.html: ✿ HyuskFocus session
components.css: .ds-library { width: 264px; padding: 22px 16px 16px; background: #242a30; color: #f2f4f5; font: 14px/1.35 system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-brand { display: block; margin-bottom: 18px; font-size: 26px; font-weight: 800; } .ds-new, .ds-search, .ds-selected { display: block; box-sizing: border-box; width: 100%; margin-bottom: 12px; padding: 9px 12px; border: 0; border-radius: 9px; background: #343d46; color: #f2f4f5; font: inherit; text-align: left; } .ds-selected { background: #215bc9; color: #fff; }

components.name: Run workflow button
components.description: Primary action to run the saved workflow selected in the editor.
components.css: .ds-run { border: 0; border-radius: 9px; padding: 8px 18px; background: #215bc9; color: #fff; font: 700 14px system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-run:hover, .ds-run:focus-visible { background: #316ddd; } .ds-run:active { background: #194aa5; } .ds-run:disabled { background: #343d46; color: #9aa0a6; }

components.name: Workflow module
components.description: Editable action row with position, kind, command, and reorder affordances.
components.html: 1Open
components.css: .ds-module { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; padding: 12px; border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.14); border-radius: 12px; background: #34383d; color: #f2f4f5; font: 14px/1.35 system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-number { display: grid; place-items: center; min-width: 30px; min-height: 36px; padding: 0 6px; border-radius: 9px; background: #dbe6ff; color: #123575; font-size: 18px; font-weight: 800; } .ds-kind { min-width: 54px; font-size: 12px; } .ds-command { flex: 1; min-width: 0; padding: 8px; border: 0; border-radius: 8px; background: #45484d; color: #f2f4f5; font: inherit; } .ds-step { min-width: 28px; min-height: 28px; border: 0; border-radius: 8px; background: #45484d; color: #f2f4f5; } .ds-step:hover, .ds-step:focus-visible { background: #56616d; }

narrative.overview:
Hyusk's workflow studio is a compact instrument for inspecting and running real desktop routines. It pairs a dark graphite library rail with a native themed GTK editor, where each ordered action becomes a numbered module. The butterfly remains the sole brand mark; native GNOME controls and type keep the experience grounded in the desktop.

The native app's first viewport is organized around the work: a searchable routine list at left, an expansive editor at right, and a fixed feedback footer below. Blue marks transport and selection, while module number keys use category colors to help users scan a sequence without making color the only label. Scheduling stays in an expandable section so the ordered actions remain the focus. The GNOME Shell companion offers quick status and workflow controls, while the Hyusk service remains the execution authority.
keyCharacteristics: Graphite sidebar and native, theme-aware GTK editor surfaces.
Ordered steps presented as clearly numbered, category-colored modules.
Fixed status footer and explicit save-before-run behavior for edited drafts.
Compact GNOME Shell indicator and searchable quick-run menu.

rules.name: The Labeled Module Rule
rules.body: Category color supports scanning, while every step also keeps its number and readable kind label.

rules.name: The Transport Rule
rules.body: Reserve saturated blue for selection and direct run actions; don't use it as decoration.

dos: Do preserve GTK4/libadwaita controls and their active theme behavior.
Do keep the rail, numbered modules, fixed feedback footer, and expandable scheduling hierarchy.
Do keep step numbers and text labels visible when using category colors.
Do make draft status and the save-before-run requirement explicit.
Do send execution requests to the Hyusk service; keep the editor as the authoring and control surface.
Do treat dedicated browser automation as a separate CDP browser profile, isolated from the user's normal browser profile.
donts: Don't replace native controls with fake hardware switches or decorative console chrome.
Don't let scheduling crowd out the ordered action sequence.
Don't rely on color alone for module kind, agent state, validation, or execution feedback.
Don't imply edits are saved or runnable when the selected workflow still has an unsaved draft.
Don't present an illustrative review capture as the user's actual workflow data or as proof of a live GNOME render.
